name: Kitchen Remodel Timelines and Scheduling
headline: Kitchen Remodel Timelines and Scheduling
articleBody: Project duration depends on scope, permitting, material lead times, and whether hidden conditions appear. A cosmetic kitchen update may take several weeks once work starts, while a full gut remodel with layout changes, inspections, cabinetry fabrication, and specialty finishes can extend to several months. Contractor and remodeling industry guidance commonly notes that lead times for custom cabinets, stone fabrication, appliances, and permit review are often more important than demolition time itself. In Los Angeles County, the schedule can stretch further if the project requires multiple inspections, structural engineering, or coordination with a busy building department. The practical way to evaluate a contractor’s schedule is to ask for a phase-by-phase timeline: design finalization, permitting, ordering, demo, rough-in, inspections, finish installation, punch list, and final sign-off. Homeowners should also ask what items are on the critical path, because a delayed cabinet order or backordered appliance can hold up the entire closeout. A realistic schedule includes contingency for concealed work and does not promise a fixed completion date without conditions. For buyers, the key question is not only “how long,” but “what could move the date, and how will the contractor communicate those changes?
